properties.headline: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued July 29 at 8:14PM MDT until July 29 at 8:15PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
The storm which prompted the warning has weakened below severe
limits, and no longer poses an immediate threat to life or property.
Therefore, the warning will be allowed to expire.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued July 29 at 8:11PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
At 810 PM MDT, Doppler radar was tracking a strong thunderstorm 17
miles northwest of Parachute, or 45 miles northeast of Grand
Junction, moving northeast at 30 mph.

HAZARD...Wind gusts up to 50 mph and half inch hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Gusty winds could knock down tree limbs and blow around
unsecured objects. Minor hail damage to vegetation is
possible.

Locations impacted include...
Rio Blanco.

This includes Colorado 13 between mile markers 9 and 21.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 8:10PM MDT until July 29 at 11:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Willow Burn Scar in...
Central Lake County in central Colorado...

* Until 1115 PM MDT.

* At 810 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms produced heavy
rain over the Willow Burn Scar. Up to 0.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall
is expected. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the Rock Creek, WIllow Creek, Rock Creek
Trail and near the Leadville National Fish Hatchery. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Willow Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Willow Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Turquoise Lake.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 7:51PM MDT until July 29 at 10:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
...FLASH FLOOD WARNING FOR THE ASPEN ACRES BURN SCAR REMAINS IN
EFFECT UNTIL 10 PM MDT THIS EVENING FOR EAST CENTRAL CUSTER AND WEST
CENTRAL PUEBLO COUNTIES...

At 751 PM MDT, At 7:47 pm, the widespread heavy rain has moved east
of the Aspen Acres burn scar. However, small showers with heavy rain
were moving across the burn scar area. Damage in Beulah has been
reported as significant and photos show homes flooded, with the water
halfway up to the roof. Cars were halfway submerged in mud and water.

FLASH FLOOD EMERGENCY for The northern and central part of the
Aspen burn scar, including Beulah. This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS
SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER GROUND NOW!

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

SOURCE...reported by emergency management.

IMPACT...This is a PARTICULARLY DANGEROUS SITUATION. SEEK HIGHER
GROUND NOW! IMMEDIATE EVACUATION for areas in and around the
Aspen Acres Burn Scar.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Beulah, San Isabel and Wetmore.

This includes the following high risk locations...
Beulah Water Intake, Northcreek Road county line to Red Mountain Camp
and Northcreek Road from Red Mountain Camp to Beulah.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 29 at 7:22PM MDT until July 29 at 10:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:

rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...A portion of west central Colorado, including the
following counties, Delta, Mesa and Montrose.

* WHEN...Until 1030 PM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry arroyos.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 720 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause arroyo and small stream
flooding. Between 0.4 and 0.8 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Escalante Creek and Dry Fork Escalante Creek.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Escalante Forks.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
